saints.name: St. Dominic
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A Castilian canon who founded the Order of Preachers to meet heresy with learning, poverty, and the Word of God…
biography: Dominic was born about 1170 at Caleruega in Old Castile, the son of Felix Guzman and Jane of Aza. After ten years of study at Palencia, where he once sold his books to feed the starving, he became a canon regular of the cathedral of Osma.

In 1203 he accompanied his bishop, Diego of Osma, on an embassy to Denmark, and passing through Toulouse beheld the ruin wrought by the Albigensian heresy. There he resolved to answer error not by the sword but by learned preaching in evangelical poverty, and in 1206 founded at Prouille a convent for converted women.

In 1215 he gathered his first friars at Toulouse; when the Fourth Lateran Council barred new religious orders, he adopted the ancient Rule of St. Augustine, and Honorius III confirmed the Order of Preachers on 22 December 1216. He soon sent his friars to the universities of Paris and Bologna.

He died at Bologna on 6 August 1221 and was canonized by Gregory IX in 1234. Long tradition associates him with the spread of the Rosary, and because early biographers tell that a star was seen upon his forehead at his baptism, he is honoured as patron of astronomers.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 4 August
